lens: syntax alignment — where the .mn corpus departs from docs/SYNTAX.md (boot c8ba5799 + the uncommitted L-C tree)
summary:
I measured the corpus with the medium's own read verbs. All 119 mentl processes ran one at a time, each answer was saved whole and read whole, and the MemAvailable floor was checked before every run.

**(1) Effect-op parameters, the class Morgan anchored on.**
- Method: `mentl where <module> <Effect>` for every effect the doc rosters list, 93 runs.
- Result: 88 effects, 391 ops, 437 parameters rendered `_: T`, 1 named (`Derivative.d(v: Float)`).
- I read three effects from source:
  - InferCtx (infer.mn:62-134): 23 ops, 17 unnamed.
  - Console (io.mn:121): 1 unnamed.
  - StateWalk (types.mn:1441): 1 named.
- Total: 455 of 457 op parameters are unnamed, across 91 effects and 416 ops (src/types 200, lib 121, other src 134).
- `provider of fs_write_file` and `provider of graph_bind` show that the names exist in the arm binders: wasi_filesystem binds `path`, `bytes`, `fd`, `old_p`, `new_p`.
- `where` also renders `-> ()` on 149 of the 391 ops.

**(2) The comment paradigm.** 18 `prose NEEDLE` questions over the src/main.mn link:

| Needle | Comments |
|---|---|
| `───` | 372 |
| walkthrough | 32 |
| `(spec ` | 30 |
| `SYNTAX.md:` | 14 |
| DELETED | 34 |
| `List<` | 7 |
| `seed's` | 32 |
| `handle {` | 2 |
| no longer | 23 |
| previously | 2 |
| legacy | 1 |
| `Until 20` | 19 |
| `drift-audit: ignore` | 134 |
| `═══` | 1 |

- Deduplicated unions: 145 archaeology comments, 44 lifecycle comments, 516 decorated, archaeological or lifecycle comments in all.
- `V1` (18 hits) and `used to` (84 hits) are not reported as counts: the facet is substring-only, so `V1` matches inside `RV128` and `used to` matches the purpose sense.

**(3) Lambdas.** From the census earlier in this session:
- anonymous: 279
- eta: 0
- effectful-lambda: 220
- underscore-retain, positive-row, default-param: 0
- `refs of arm_list_of` shows that format.mn:464 renders a lambda as an arm list only when its body is `match p {…}`.

**(4) Formatter scope and conservation, read from source.**
- fmt_run (main.mn:433-487) renders and writes one module.
- cli.mn:224-231 requires a target.
- lost_atoms (format.mn:1440-1464) is a multiset, so a render that drops a duplicate import line would be refused.

**(5) Stage Law.**
- lib/dsp/signal.mn documents "data-first for |> chains".
- feedback.mn:84 needs the wrapper `((y) => lp(y, cutoff))`.
- `refs of clip|gain|mix`: 0 on main; on Pulse only one direct `mix` call, plus `gain` hits that are a parameter and a local of that name.

**(6) Imports.** The imports facet reports 258 edges. Both of infer's duplicate lines are marked "used", and two false DEAD verdicts remain against `ty_string`'s 24 references.

**(7) The course seed.** The whole of examples/pulse/render/main.mn read by hand:
- 43 base-typed parameters on 25 declaration lines, and 18 `-> Float` returns
- 7 `0.0 - x`
- 17 binder lambdas in `<~` recurrences
- three literal spellings where the prose disagrees with the code

**Shape of the answer.** Nearly every departure is the same disease: a fact the graph already holds (a name, a projection, an equivalence, a rule) is restated somewhere the gates cannot see — a comment, a positional slot, a second renderer, or a hand-kept line. The fixes are graph projections plus census bounds, and most of them delete code.

findings.title: `mentl fmt` is single-file and target-required, so there is no project-wide canonical form
findings.current: `VerbSpec("fmt", "<path>", (a) => if len(a) >= 3 { Invocation(VFmt(a[2])) } else { ParseError("fmt needs a target: mentl fmt <path>") }, …)`. fmt_run renders only `driver_module_ast(ast_all, entry_module)` and writes one path. Bare `mentl fmt` is a ParseError, and no project or `--check` mode exists. The render keys literals by value, so Pulse's prose says `Sample(48_000)`, `delay(12_000)` and `!Sample(44_100)` while its code says `48000`, `12000` and `44100` (`Hβ.fmt.literal-spelling-is-intent`).
findings.ideal:
Bare `mentl fmt` is the project's canonical projection (cargo-style, and stronger):
- The project is the directory's modules, or the entry's import closure.
- Every module whose source differs from its canonical render is rendered.
- Modules whose source hash equals their last canonical render are skipped, so the cost is the changed set (§5.O).
- The write is atomic: no file is written if any module's render fails the conservation proof.
- One line is printed per module written.
- `--check` is the same answer as a `verify` bound.

The canonicalizations are exactly the graph-preserving band: layout, braces, duplicate imports, `-> ()`, decoration runs, and the import-block projection. Spelling the graph should carry, such as digit grouping, is preserved, not erased.
findings.law: SYNTAX principle 1 (layout is projection, never contract). §5.O: the cost of an operation is the size of its answer. The conservation law in format.mn:1440 ("what a render may never lose").
findings.evidence: Read cli.mn:224-232 and main.mn:433-487. `refs of VFmt` → cli:228 and main:147 only. Read all of Pulse main.mn for the three spelling divergences.
findings.class_size: 1 verb. Every module in the tree is formatted only by an explicit single-file run.

findings.title: Duplicate imports reach no gate; the imports facet double-counts them, and the conservation census would refuse fmt's fix
sites: src/canon.mn:17 (let ty_string — the target of two false DEAD verdicts)
findings.current: The imports facet reports "258 import edge(s)" and lists `used infer -> import io` twice and `used infer -> import verify` twice. It gives `DEAD infer -> import canon` and `DEAD parser -> import canon` although `refs of ty_string` returns 24 references (23 in infer, 1 in parser); the facet misses module-let references. The fixture states the semantics: "drawing an edge that exists is a no-op, because that is what an edge is". So the graph is right, the page is redundant, and nothing says so. lost_atoms is "a count rather than a set": an fmt that dropped the second `import verify` would leave one `verify` atom unpaid and refuse to write.
findings.ideal: A duplicate import is a redundant form (SYNTAX principle 2). `E_DuplicateImport` is reported by `check` as a refusal (Morgan: a syntax error) with a MachineApplicable fix that fmt applies. The conservation census learns stated equivalences: a canonicalization names each atom it removes and the surviving node that still carries it, generalizing lost_atoms_beside's `stated` list. Beyond that, the import block itself becomes a projection (see root design R3).
findings.law: SYNTAX Governing principle 2 ("If two syntactic forms produce the same graph, one is rejected", :66). The format-liftable band ("MachineApplicable ∧ the redundant form has no graph node").
findings.evidence: Read infer.mn:1-56, the imports facet answer, `refs of ty_string`, canon.mn, and format.mn:1440-1490.
findings.gate: Arm E_DuplicateImport at wheel-zero, after the two infer lines are removed. A `verify` bound on DEAD imports at 0, once the facet reads module-let references. A fixture where fmt removes a duplicate and the conservation gate passes.
findings.class_size: 2 duplicate lines on the wheel (infer); 2 false DEAD verdicts; 258 facet edges counted per statement.

findings.title: The Stage Law is inverted in the library the course imports, in the prelude, and in SYNTAX's own examples
sites: lib/dsp/feedback.mn:32,43,83-84,99 (stage(x, cutoff) and the wrapper lambda)
lib/prelude.mn:347,378,411,418 (reduce(xs, f), scanl(xs, init, f), nth(xs, n, default), clamp(x, lo, hi))
findings.current:
signal.mn:3-5 describes "the pipeable pure-processor vocabulary (clip / gain / mix …) and the DSP effect, data-first for `|>` chains (x |> gain(0.8) |> soft_clip)", over `fn gain(x: Float, factor: Float)` and `fn clip(x: Float, threshold: Float)`.
- SYNTAX's fill rule ("x |> f(a) fills f(a)'s remaining hole") binds 0.8 to `x` and pipes into `factor`.
- For clip, the same rule makes `-2.0 |> clip(0.5)` compute `clamp(0.5, 2.0, -2.0)` = -2.0, where the answer should be -0.5. This is derived from the rule and not run; the read-only lens forbids `run`.
- Nothing executes the idiom: `refs of clip|gain|mix` = 0 on the main link. On Pulse there is one direct `mix(echo, dry, 0.35)`, and the `gain` hits are a parameter and a local of that name.
- feedback.mn:84 has to write `x |> dc |> ((y) => lp(y, cutoff)) |> soft_clip`, because the filter stage is (x, cutoff).
findings.ideal:
Configuration first, datum last, wherever a value flows:
- `gain(factor, x)`, `clip(threshold, x)`, filter stages `stage(cutoff, x)`;
- `reduce(f, xs)`, `scanl(f, init, xs)`, `nth(n, default, xs)`, `clamp(lo, hi, x)`.

Then `x |> dc |> lp(cutoff) |> soft_clip` and `x |> clamp(0, 255)` need no `??` and no wrapper. SYNTAX's own clamp examples adopt the datum-last signature, so its `??` example becomes a stage that genuinely is not a stage.
findings.law: SYNTAX §«The Stage Law»: "a `??` inside a pipe becomes a SIGNAL … the fix is the SIGNATURE, never decoration at N call sites". "No `??`, no wrapper lambdas, no argument gymnastics."
findings.evidence: Read signal.mn:1-100 and 140-200, feedback.mn whole, prelude.mn:326-420, Pulse main.mn whole, and the SYNTAX lines by grep. Six `refs of` answers.
findings.gate:
1. A census shape `CsPipeShim` (a pipe stage that is a lambda or carries an explicit `??`), counted on `verify` and ratcheted.
2. A teach narration `T_StageOrder` at a declaration when its pipe sites wrap or hole the same parameter.
3. A medium-authored reorder, run as a tighten-style sweep: the signature plus every call site read off `refs of`, positional calls permuted, labeled calls untouched. It is proven by re-judging inside the D4 checkpoint bracket.
findings.class_size: 13 datum-first signatures read. The class is uncounted: there is no census for it (verb gap).

- Lifecycle needles: no longer 23, previously 2, legacy 1, `Until 20` 19 — 44 distinct.

findings.ideal: SYNTAX §Comments: no decoration ("the declaration's name IS the heading"); "a comment shows what IS, not what was"; a residue names its retirement condition; "Not a gate. A comment adds, never silences". Sections are a projection (doc groups by module and kind). History lives in LEDGER and git. A mechanism claim is checked through its edges. A gate is never muted by prose: the 134 markers suppress text-level drift rows (keyword-looking string literals, message strings, a one-shot `++ [x]`) that a structural census reads correctly, because a string literal is `text` and a non-loop concat is not an accumulator.
findings.law: SYNTAX «What a comment is NOT» and «What a comment TRENDS TO». CLAUDE.md: a law that can become a gate must; prose never overrides one.
findings.evidence: 18 `prose NEEDLE` answers over src/main.mn, read whole, with span unions computed from the saved answers. Read the sampled sites. Sampled suppressions (21 of 134) were foreign-keyword string literals, DiagKind message strings, and non-loop `++ [x]`.

1. fmt strips box-drawing decoration runs. This is graph-preserving: the prose line survives, and the conservation census counts lines.
2. `mentl verify` carries prose-census bounds ratcheted to 0 for `Until 20`, `no longer`, `previously`, `walkthrough`, `(spec `, `seed's`, `DELETED`, and box-drawing.
3. The `drift-audit: ignore` count is bounded and falls as each muted text row becomes a structural census shape. At zero, the marker's grammar deletes, and a comment can no longer silence anything.

findings.title: The binder-lambda residue is wider than SYNTAX claims, and the census misses its commonest shape
findings.current:
- Census: anonymous 279, eta 0, effectful-lambda 220.
- `lambda_is_eta` requires the arguments to equal the parameters exactly, so references-with-a-hole written as mints count nowhere: `(a) => req_target(a, VCheck, "…")` (cli:149/154/178), `(row) => dot(row, x)` (tensor:26), `((y) => lp(y, cutoff))` (feedback:84).
- fmt renders an arm list only when arm_list_of matches, which needs a sole parameter, a `match p {…}` body, and p not free in the arms. So `(x) => x + 1` keeps its binder, although SYNTAX §«The residue» says a sole-parameter lambda renders as its arms. SYNTAX's own `<~` example (:961) uses the binder form.
- Six cli builders ignore their argument: `(a) => Invocation(VSession)` and five like it.
- effectful-lambda now counts allocation (R0i), so cli's 20 constructors all count as "effectful".
findings.ideal:
Two operations, as SYNTAX says:
- a reference with holes: `dot(??, x)`, `scalar_mul(??, b)`, `req_target(??, VCheck, msg)`, and `lp(cutoff)` once the stage is datum-last;
- or an arm list `{ p => body }`.

The parser builds a one-arm list with an irrefutable binder pattern as the same LambdaExpr the binder form builds: one graph, no match node. fmt then renders every sole-parameter mint as `{ x => x + 1 }`, and resugar_head's single-parameter path deletes. Multi-parameter lambdas become references (`fold(0, add, xs)`), per `Hβ.syntax.multi-param-lambda-is-a-reference`.
findings.law: SYNTAX §«Function literals» (a function value is reached by exactly two operations). Anchor 6.
findings.evidence: Census answers for anonymous, eta and effectful-lambda. `refs of arm_list_of` → query:1798, format:665, format:464. Read parser.mn:2518-2557, format.mn:440-489 and 650-680, query.mn:1788-1832, and cli.mn:140-268.
findings.gate:
1. A census shape `CsPartialEta`: a lambda whose body is one call that uses each parameter exactly once as a whole argument. A medium-authored rewrite turns it into the reference-with-hole, bounded to 0.
2. `CsSoleParamBinder`, format-liftable to 0 once the parser equivalence lands.
3. effectful-lambda excludes the construction charge, or retires as a proxy.
findings.class_size: 279 anonymous functions; partial-eta not counted (verb gap); 20 in cli alone.

findings.title: Three projections of one declaration head disagree with each other and with SYNTAX
sites: src/format.mn:1221-1242 (render_effect_ops: TUnit → ""; render_op_param: a bare type for `_`)
`mentl where` (`_: T`, and `-> ()` on 149 of 391 ops)
`mentl doc` (every effect as `E : ()`, e.g. `CursorRead : ()`, `DiagBank : ()`; instances as `WASI(t148105@e167038)`)
findings.current:
One op is spelled four ways:
- source and fmt: `fs_write_file(String, String)`
- where: `fs_write_file(_: String, _: String) -> ()`
- doc: `Filesystem : ()`, with no ops at all
- where on fmt_run: `WASI(a)`; doc: `WASI(t148105@e167038)`

`spawn`'s thunk row variable and its type variable both render as `a`. `Any` is not a SYNTAX token. SYNTAX itself contradicts: :1600 accepts both `-> ()` and its omission, while :1625 rejects `resume(())` by "No redundant form", and :1631 writes `tick() -> ()`.
findings.ideal: One head projection — the formatter's head render — serves fmt, where, doc, the space View and hover, and every rendered head re-parses to the declaration it came from. `-> ()` is a format-liftable redundant form that no projection writes. Row variables use a lowercase alphabet disjoint from the head's type variables: the case rule extended to row position, e.g. `spawn(f: () -> a with e)`. `Any` and `t…@e…` never render. `doc` lists an effect's ops.
findings.law: SYNTAX Governing principle 2 (:66). Carried-Truth: one home per projection. SYNTAX's case rule (lowercase in type position is a parameter).
findings.evidence: 88 where answers, the format.mn:1190-1260 read, doc rosters from this session, and the SYNTAX lines by grep.
findings.gate:
1. A round-trip board leg: for every declaration in the link, parse(where-head) and parse(fmt-head) equal the declaration (`Hβ.fmt.render-must-parse-to-the-same-tree`, applied to heads).
2. A census of explicit `-> ()` at 0.
3. SYNTAX:1596-1600 rewritten to name `-> ()` a format-liftable redundant form, and :1631 corrected.
findings.class_size: 149 `-> ()` renders across 391 where-ops; all 91 effects render without ops in doc.

findings.current:
Pulse scene 1, read whole:

One ownership-marker position is chosen; the other parses and is format-lifted.
findings.law: SYNTAX is the authority ("where they disagree, the parser is wrong" — and so is any example). The teachability face of PLAN §11 Phase 11.3 ("the surface IS the course").

findings.title: Positional products whose field meanings live in comments
sites: src/types.mn:1370-1375 (type Graph = Graph(Int, [(ValidSpan, Int)]), with field docs after the type)
src/infer.mn:64-68 (inf_exit_fn() -> ([(EffName, Bool, EConn)], Int, EffRow, Span))
src/types.mn:4407 (ls_enter_frame(_: String, _: List(String), _: List(Int), _: List(String), _: List(Int), _: Int))
findings.current: `type VerbSpec = VerbSpec(String, String, ([String]) -> EntryHandlerInvocation, String)`, documented by a comment: "A VerbSpec carries the verb's name, its argument hint …, the BUILDER …, and its one-line description". The two leading Strings differ only by position. The usage string is restated three times per verb: in the hint, in `len(a) >= 3`, and in the ParseError text. `ls_enter_frame` passes two parallel (List(String), List(Int)) pairs.
findings.ideal: Named records: `type VerbSpec = {name: String, hint: String, build: ([String]) -> EntryHandlerInvocation, describe: String}`. Better still, the verb's argument grammar becomes data (an ADT of argument shapes) from which the builder, the hint and the error are projected. Op results with three or four positional fields become records. Parallel lists become one list of records (drift 7). Field documentation attaches to field names.

root_designs: R1 — ONE PARAMETER-PRODUCT GRAMMAR FOR EVERY HEAD. A fn's parameters, an arm list's pattern, an effect op's parameters, a handler's config, an effect's instance arguments, a constructor's fields and an op's multi-field result are one product: keyed by name, typed by inference unless the type is a decision, defaulted and marked the same way, and rendered by one head projection. This deletes the bare-type op grammar (455 unnamed parameters), `op_scheme_param`'s invented `_0` and `_1`, `render_op_param`'s `_` branch, and comment-held field tables such as VerbSpec's and the WASI comments. In exchange the medium gains labeled performs, arms checked by name, field-level documentation, Why-chains through op parameters as binders, and named fields in the multi-shot yield record a time-travel debugger reads.

R2 — `mentl fmt` IS THE PROJECT'S CANONICAL PROJECTION, cargo-style and stronger.
- Bare `fmt` renders every module of the project (the directory or the entry's import closure) whose source differs from its canonical render. A module whose source hash matches its last render is skipped, so the cost is the changed set.
- It writes atomically, under the conservation proof.
- Its canonicalizations are exactly the graph-preserving band: layout, braces, duplicate imports, `-> ()`, decoration runs, an exact `0 - x`, and the import-block projection (R3).
- Each canonicalization is also a census bound on `verify`. So `check` and CI refuse a non-canonical tree — the 'syntax error' Morgan asked for — and fmt is that error's MachineApplicable fix.
- The conservation census learns stated equivalences: each canonicalization names the atoms it removes and the node that keeps them. Without that, the multiset census refuses every deduplication.

R3 — THE IMPORT BLOCK IS A PROJECTION OF REFERENCE EDGES (A4's law applied to modules). fmt writes one sorted line per declaring module the references reach. An authored import survives only where it decides something, such as a selective set narrowing a collision. Duplicates, dead imports and missing imports (E_MissingImport) become unsayable on the canonical page. This requires the imports facet to read module-let references; today it calls infer→canon DEAD over 24 references.

R5 — ONE HEAD PROJECTION WITH A ROUND-TRIP GATE. fmt, where, doc, the space View and hover render every declaration head through the formatter's head render. parse(render(head)) == head is a board leg over the whole link. Row variables and type variables render in disjoint lowercase alphabets: SYNTAX's case rule extended to row position. `-> ()`, `Any` and `t…@e…` never render. doc lists an effect's ops.

R6 — THE COMMENT PARADIGM MADE MECHANICAL.
- A module-lede slot.
- Field docs attach to field names.
- Box-drawing decoration is a format-lift.
- Lifecycle and archaeology needles become prose-census bounds on `verify`.
- Comment edges resolve against the project's declarations: no narrow-link noise, no `node N` owners, one report per edge.
- A comment never silences a gate: the 134 `drift-audit: ignore` markers delete as the text rows they mute become structural census shapes, which already distinguish a string literal (`text`) from code and a one-shot `++` from an accumulator.

R7 — THE PROJECT IS THE UNIT OF EVERY GATE. `check`, `fmt` and `verify` operate on every module of the project and report each diagnostic once, at its own module. A claim such as 'the wheel carries zero diagnostics' is measured over all modules, not the entry. SYNTAX's fenced examples, and the course (Pulse's chapters, then Wasatch), are battery members under the same bounds, born canonical.
verb_gaps: No facet enumerates every effect with its ops and parameter names. `doc` renders an effect as `E : ()`; `where` answers one name per process, so measuring the corpus took 93 separate processes; `variants NAME` gives arities, not names.
The census roster is not listable: `mentl query src/main.mn census` → 'unknown query'.

No census shapes exist for: unnamed op parameters, positional products, partial-eta (a reference written as a mint), a lambda or `??` in a pipe stage (the Stage Law's signal), base-type inventory annotations, `0 - x`, explicit `-> ()`, duplicate imports, misattached ledes, and ops whose providers' write behaviour contradicts the effect name.
`census underscore-retain` counts `let _x =` only, not underscore-named parameters or pattern binders.
`prose NEEDLE` is substring-only: `V1` matches inside `RV128`, and `used to` matches the purpose sense. A word- or token-bounded form is needed.
`refs of NAME` is keyed by name: on Pulse, `refs of gain` returns a parameter and a local that happen to be called `gain`, not the library function (which has 0 references).

`imports` gives no duplicate verdict (its 258 edges count infer's two duplicate lines as two used edges) and misses module-let references (false DEAD for infer→canon and parser→canon against `ty_string`'s 24 references).
`fmt` requires a target, writes exactly one module, and has neither a project mode nor `--check`.
`check <entry>` scopes to the entry module; no project-wide check exists (graph ×6, infer ×1 and lexer ×1 T_OwnUnconsumed never reach the board).
`where <module>` prints the module's narrow-link comment-ref warnings before its answer (34 for types.mn). Those warnings name anonymous owners as `node N` and repeat once per backtick occurrence.
`doc` misses module lets (`doc src/canon.mn` is empty) and renders non-parseable instance heads (`WASI(t148105@e167038)`).
The lede projection truncates at abbreviations ('…repr (e.g.' on emit_binop_repr_unsupported).
